Title: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection in SimpleXML Converter
Analysis:
The `SimpleXmlResponseBodyConverter` class in the SimpleXML converter module is vulnerable to XML External Entity (XXE) injection. By default, `org.simpleframework.xml.Serializer` (usually implemented by `Persister`) does not disable external DTDs or external entity loading. This allows a remote attacker to supply a malicious XML response body containing an external entity (e.g., pointing to sensitive local files like `/etc/passwd` or using `http://` schemas to trigger Server-Side Request Forgery/SSRF) when Retrofit processes the API response.

Because this converter relies entirely on the default behavior of the `Serializer` passed to it (or constructed by default in `SimpleXmlConverterFactory.create()`), and because there is no sanitization or secure parser configuration in `SimpleXmlResponseBodyConverter.convert()`, an attacker-controlled HTTP response will parse and resolve external entities upon deserialization.

**Conceptual Exploit Payload:**
An attacker-controlled HTTP server returns the following XML response to a Retrofit client configured with `SimpleXmlConverterFactory`:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE root [
  <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">
]>
<user>
  <username>&xxe;</username>
  <email>attacker@example.com</email>
</user>
```

When `serializer.read()` executes in `SimpleXmlResponseBodyConverter.convert()`, the underlying XML parser resolves the `&xxe;` entity, reading the contents of `/etc/passwd` and populating the parsed object with it, leading to sensitive data exposure or SSRF.
